opportunities.title: Detention + appointment exception manager
opportunities.wedge: Detect likely detention before arrival, capture cause/evidence and coordinate shipper, carrier and driver actions while the delay can still be changed.
opportunities.buyer: Carriers, brokers and shippers with truckload volume.
opportunities.painMoment: The truck is waiting, the driver's legal clock is burning, and nobody owns the exception.
opportunities.firstTest: Instrument one lane or facility for four weeks and measure detention hours avoided plus dispute evidence captured.
riskNotes: Driver-location data needs careful privacy controls.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong real-time exception and multi-actor workflow fit.

evidence.title: FMCSA Split Duty Period pilot and detention context
evidence.note: FMCSA explicitly cites unreasonable detention times as a problem affecting driver working conditions and HOS constraints.

evidence.title: CSCMP State of Logistics 2026
evidence.note: The sector remains shaped by labor/productivity constraints and a need for end-to-end visibility.

opportunities.title: End-to-end exception visibility
opportunities.wedge: Fuse shipment milestones, inventory, ETA uncertainty and human ownership into an exception-first control layer rather than another dashboard of everything.
opportunities.buyer: Shippers, 3PLs and logistics providers.
opportunities.painMoment: We have tracking data everywhere but still discover the important failure after the customer does.
opportunities.firstTest: Build an exception-only view for one customer account and measure earlier detection plus manual status-check reduction.
riskNotes: Data integrations are the product moat and the implementation burden.
opportunities.fitNote: Near-direct fit for information architecture, agentic coordination and exception UX.

evidence.title: CSCMP State of Logistics 2026
evidence.note: The report prioritizes end-to-end visibility, resilience and digital/automation ROI.

evidence.title: CSCMP research and surveys
evidence.note: Logistics benchmarking centers on costs, capacity and evolving supply-chain constraints.

opportunities.title: Warehouse automation ROI preflight
opportunities.wedge: Compare labor constraints, throughput, error rates, SKU profile and capital requirements before committing to automation hardware or software.
opportunities.buyer: Warehouse operators, distributors and 3PLs.
opportunities.painMoment: Every vendor says automation will pay back, but the operation has no neutral model of where it actually should.
opportunities.firstTest: Run five paid preflights with no hardware resale incentive and compare recommendations with subsequent investment decisions.
riskNotes: Facility engineering constraints need domain partners.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong neutral diagnostic/product-strategy fit with warehouse engineering partnership.

evidence.title: CSCMP State of Logistics 2026
evidence.note: Companies are accelerating automation due to labor constraints and are urged to focus on digital/automation ROI.

evidence.title: CSCMP Logistics 2030 research
evidence.note: Warehousing, distribution and future logistics technology are explicit long-term research areas.

opportunities.title: Trade + landed-cost scenario workflow
opportunities.wedge: Turn tariff, routing, supplier and inventory assumptions into scenario comparisons that operations, finance and sourcing can all inspect.
opportunities.buyer: Importers, manufacturers and supply-chain teams.
opportunities.painMoment: The policy changed, but nobody knows the actual cost until purchasing, freight, inventory and finance reconcile separate spreadsheets.
opportunities.firstTest: Model one product family across three sourcing/routing scenarios and compare with manual planning time.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong complex-decision and data-synthesis fit.

evidence.title: CSCMP State of Logistics 2026
evidence.note: Trade-flow and geoeconomic realignment are identified as structural logistics forces with no near-term resolution.

evidence.title: CSCMP 2026 report highlights
evidence.note: The 2026 logistics outlook emphasizes resilience, capital discipline and intelligence.

opportunities.title: Asset-productivity exception radar
opportunities.wedge: Show which trailers, trucks, warehouse zones or transport assets are idle for preventable reasons and route the blocker to an owner.
opportunities.buyer: Asset-heavy carriers, 3PLs and logistics operators.
opportunities.painMoment: We keep buying capacity while existing capacity spends too much time waiting or moving empty.
opportunities.firstTest: Analyze one operation's asset state history and resolve the top three preventable idle patterns.
riskNotes: Operational constraints can be misclassified as avoidable.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong exception analytics and agentic operations fit.

evidence.title: CSCMP State of Logistics 2026
evidence.note: The report explicitly recommends prioritizing asset productivity over footprint expansion.

evidence.title: FMCSA detention pilot context
evidence.note: Detention is one concrete example of capacity being consumed without productive movement.

opportunities.title: Downtime root-cause + recovery workflow
opportunities.wedge: Join machine events, maintenance history, operator notes and production context into a verified incident timeline with next actions.
opportunities.buyer: Plant operations and maintenance leaders.
opportunities.painMoment: The line is down and five teams each have a different theory of why.
opportunities.firstTest: Replay ten downtime events from one plant, then pilot live incident capture and compare mean time to recovery.
riskNotes: Models must never directly command unsafe actions.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent high-value incident UX and synthesis fit with OT partner required.

evidence.title: NIST manufacturing cyber recovery guide
evidence.note: NIST emphasizes minimizing manufacturing downtime and restoring operations after incidents.

evidence.title: NIST OT backup guidance
evidence.note: Backup failures can produce extended downtime, financial losses and safety incidents.

opportunities.title: OT cyber recovery readiness diagnostic
opportunities.wedge: Map critical OT assets, backups, restoration dependencies, roles and tested recovery paths before an incident forces improvisation.
opportunities.buyer: Manufacturers with industrial control systems.
opportunities.painMoment: We have security controls, but do not know whether the plant can actually recover if OT is disrupted.
opportunities.firstTest: Run a tabletop and technical evidence review on one production cell; produce a prioritized recovery-gap map.
opportunities.fitNote: HAAM can structure the workflow but should partner with OT cybersecurity specialists.

evidence.title: NIST SP 1800-41 manufacturing incident response and recovery
evidence.note: NIST says ICS cyber incidents threaten safety, production and economic performance and require recovery capabilities.

evidence.title: NIST OT Backup Quick Start Guide
evidence.note: Reliable OT backup and recovery are presented as essential operational-resilience capabilities.

opportunities.title: Digital-twin interoperability + trust preflight
opportunities.wedge: Assess whether a proposed digital twin has the data contracts, validation, uncertainty handling and interoperability needed for the decision it is supposed to support.
opportunities.buyer: Manufacturers investing in digital twins and smart-factory programs.
opportunities.painMoment: The demo is impressive, but we still cannot tell whether the twin is trustworthy enough for an operational decision.
opportunities.firstTest: Audit one existing twin against its claimed decisions and identify missing validation/interoperability evidence.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong systems/verification design fit with domain expert collaboration.

evidence.title: NIST Digital Twins Workshops Summary Report 2026
evidence.note: NIST identifies interoperability, verification/validation/uncertainty, cybersecurity and workforce readiness as persistent barriers.

evidence.title: NIST manufacturing recovery work
evidence.note: NIST's manufacturing work emphasizes operational resilience in connected OT environments.

opportunities.title: Nonconformance + CAPA evidence orchestrator
opportunities.wedge: Connect inspection results, defects, process context, corrective actions and verification into a closed evidence trail with only the true exceptions escalated.
opportunities.buyer: Quality leaders in regulated or high-cost manufacturing.
opportunities.painMoment: The defect is visible, but finding root cause and proving the corrective action worked spans too many systems and people.
opportunities.firstTest: Run one defect family through a unified CAPA workflow and measure closure time plus repeat defects.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent evidence-workflow fit with quality-system specialist partnership.

evidence.title: NIST digital twin and validation barriers
evidence.note: Verification, validation and uncertainty are central trust challenges in modern manufacturing systems.

evidence.title: NIST manufacturing operational resilience
evidence.note: Connected industrial systems require robust, evidence-based resilience practices.

opportunities.title: Frontline knowledge capture + troubleshooting memory
opportunities.wedge: Turn operator fixes, maintenance notes and expert reasoning into searchable, equipment-specific troubleshooting memory with provenance.
opportunities.buyer: Plants facing experienced-worker retirement or multi-shift knowledge gaps.
opportunities.painMoment: The person who knows this machine is on another shift, another site, or about to retire.
opportunities.firstTest: Capture one expert technician's recurring troubleshooting cases and measure time-to-answer for less experienced staff.
riskNotes: Incorrect troubleshooting advice can affect safety.
Tacit knowledge is difficult to encode fully.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong knowledge architecture and multimodal AI fit with conservative safety boundaries.

evidence.title: NIST digital twins workshop report
evidence.note: Workforce readiness is identified as a persistent challenge in advanced manufacturing adoption.

evidence.title: NIST manufacturing resilience project
evidence.note: Operational resilience requires usable technical knowledge and recovery capabilities across teams.

opportunities.title: Returns cost + fraud optimizer
opportunities.wedge: Decide which returns should be free, paid, inspected, routed or refunded instantly based on item economics, customer history and fraud evidence.
opportunities.buyer: Omnichannel retailers and ecommerce brands.
opportunities.painMoment: The return experience drives conversion, but blanket generosity can quietly erase margin and invite abuse.
opportunities.firstTest: Replay 10,000 historical returns and compare policy outcomes with current rules, then A/B one low-risk segment.
opportunities.priceHypothesis: Basis points of returns value or US$2k-25k/mo
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent high-feedback data product opportunity.

evidence.title: NRF: nearly $850B in merchandise returns
evidence.note: Retailers name reducing return rates as a 2026 priority; 64% prioritize updating returns processes and 9% of returns are estimated fraudulent.

evidence.title: NRF Retail Fraud Taxonomy 2026
evidence.note: NRF documents evolving fraud techniques across physical and digital retail channels.

opportunities.title: Total retail loss intelligence
opportunities.wedge: Join theft, fraud, inventory errors, supply-chain loss and operational mistakes into a causal loss map instead of one lagging shrink number.
opportunities.buyer: Large retailers, asset protection and operations leaders.
opportunities.painMoment: We know the shrink number after the quarter, but not which process is leaking margin today.
opportunities.firstTest: Build a cross-source loss map for one region and validate top drivers with AP/operations teams.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong analytics/information architecture fit.

evidence.title: NRF: moving beyond shrink to total retail loss
evidence.note: NRF describes shrink as a lagging metric and promotes a broader loss model spanning theft, fraud, inventory and supply-chain failures.

evidence.title: NRF Impact of Retail Theft & Violence 2026
evidence.note: Retail fraud and external theft continue evolving across physical and digital environments.

opportunities.title: Omnichannel inventory truth + exception layer
opportunities.wedge: Surface where system inventory cannot be trusted, explain likely causes and route fixes before customers encounter phantom stock.
opportunities.buyer: Retail operations, ecommerce and inventory teams.
opportunities.painMoment: The website says it is in stock, the store says it is in stock, and nobody can actually find it.
opportunities.firstTest: Track top inventory exceptions across ten stores and measure cancellations, substitutions and manual searches.
riskNotes: Inventory errors have many physical causes.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent exception-first product and cross-system orchestration fit.

evidence.title: NRF total retail loss framework
evidence.note: Inventory inaccuracies and supply-chain disruptions are explicitly included in total retail loss.

evidence.title: NRF 2026 retail trends
evidence.note: AI, omnichannel operations and customer journey optimization remain major retail themes.

opportunities.title: Store incident + violence prevention workflow
opportunities.wedge: Combine incident patterns, location context, staffing and response playbooks into proactive but non-profiling safety operations.
opportunities.buyer: Retail asset-protection and store-operations teams.
opportunities.painMoment: Store teams need practical warning and response support without turning every customer into a risk score.
opportunities.firstTest: Map incident types and response breakdowns across one region, then test manager playbook prompts.
riskNotes: Never use protected-class profiling or opaque person-level predictions.
opportunities.fitNote: Potentially valuable operational UX, but requires strict safety/ethics boundaries.

evidence.title: NRF Impact of Retail Theft & Violence 2026
evidence.note: Retailers report continued violence concerns and investment in management/employee training and risk-intelligence technology.

evidence.title: NRF theft and violence research
evidence.note: The 2026 study frames theft and violence as persistent issues for retailers, employees and communities.

opportunities.title: AI customer-journey experiment governor
opportunities.wedge: Let retail teams test personalization, agents and automation with measurable conversion effects, guardrails and rollback instead of scattered AI pilots.
opportunities.buyer: Retail digital, ecommerce and product leaders.
opportunities.painMoment: Every vendor has an AI feature, but we cannot tell which one improves the customer journey without creating hidden risk.
opportunities.firstTest: Run one controlled AI journey experiment with explicit baseline, guardrails and rollback metrics.
opportunities.fitNote: Very strong product experimentation, AI governance and commerce UX fit.

evidence.title: NRF retail trends and predictions 2026
evidence.note: AI is described as an accelerating force in retail personalization and operational efficiency.

evidence.title: NRF returns research
evidence.note: Retailers are balancing digital growth, customer expectations and rising operational costs.

opportunities.title: AI code verification + trust layer
opportunities.wedge: Attach provenance, tests, review depth and risk classification to AI-generated changes so teams can scale use without pretending all generated code is equally trustworthy.
opportunities.buyer: Engineering organizations adopting AI coding agents.
opportunities.painMoment: AI makes code faster, but every generated change creates a new verification problem.
opportunities.firstTest: Instrument one team's AI-assisted PRs and compare review time, defects and rework by risk class.
riskNotes: Must integrate with existing CI/review systems.
opportunities.fitNote: Exceptional direct fit for AI product, developer workflow and verification design.

evidence.title: Stack Overflow: AI trust gap for developers
evidence.note: 84% use or plan to use AI tools while only 29% report trust in AI, creating a growing verification gap.

evidence.title: Stack Overflow: domain expertise still wanted
evidence.note: Developers increasingly use AI but validate it with traditional resources because trust remains a major barrier.

opportunities.title: Build/test wait-time eliminator
opportunities.wedge: Measure developer waiting across CI, tests, environments and reviews, then rank the fixes by recovered engineering time rather than infrastructure vanity metrics.
opportunities.buyer: Engineering productivity and platform teams.
opportunities.painMoment: The expensive engineer is waiting for a machine or workflow to tell them whether they can continue.
opportunities.firstTest: Instrument one repo for two weeks and quantify avoidable wait time by cause before proposing tooling changes.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent measurable developer-experience diagnostic.

evidence.title: GitHub developer experience survey
evidence.note: Developers reported waiting on builds and tests as the most time-consuming activity outside writing code.

evidence.title: GitHub AI software-team survey
evidence.note: Developers associate AI with workflow efficiency, while toolchain complexity remains a barrier in some organizations.

opportunities.title: Codebase onboarding + institutional memory
opportunities.wedge: Explain why systems are the way they are using code, PRs, incidents, docs and decision history rather than a one-shot generated architecture summary.
opportunities.buyer: Engineering teams with large or long-lived codebases.
opportunities.painMoment: The code tells me what exists, not why this weird decision exists or what will break if I remove it.
opportunities.firstTest: Onboard five engineers with a decision-linked codebase guide and compare time-to-first-safe-change.
riskNotes: Generated explanations need citations to source history.
opportunities.fitNote: Exceptional knowledge-architecture and agentic retrieval fit.

evidence.title: GitHub AI software-team survey
evidence.note: AI coding tools are associated with easier codebase understanding and onboarding, while organizations still need workflow integration.

evidence.title: Stack Overflow AI trust research
evidence.note: Developers continue to rely on domain expertise and external validation around AI-generated knowledge.

opportunities.title: Incident context + debugging orchestrator
opportunities.wedge: Assemble deploys, logs, traces, code changes, feature flags and ownership into a live incident hypothesis map with every inference linked to evidence.
opportunities.buyer: Software teams with meaningful production operations.
opportunities.painMoment: During an incident, the information exists, but it is spread across six tools and three people.
opportunities.firstTest: Replay ten incidents and compare time-to-causal-context with the existing incident workflow.
riskNotes: False causal claims can slow recovery.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent agentic synthesis and observability UX fit.

evidence.title: GitHub developer experience survey
evidence.note: Developers identify incident resolution and collaboration as areas where AI can provide material benefits.

evidence.title: Stack Overflow AI trust gap
evidence.note: Trust requires review and confidence that AI does not introduce unacceptable production risk or technical debt.

opportunities.title: Toolchain complexity + AI policy diagnostic
opportunities.wedge: Map where developers switch tools, re-enter context, wait for approvals or use unapproved AI, then simplify the workflow before buying another platform.
opportunities.buyer: CTO, platform engineering and developer-experience teams.
opportunities.painMoment: Every new tool promised productivity, and now the workflow itself is the thing developers fight.
opportunities.firstTest: Observe one team end-to-end for two weeks and quantify context switches, duplicate steps and shadow-AI use.
riskNotes: Recommendations can threaten incumbent internal tools.
opportunities.fitNote: Direct systems/interaction design and workflow-diagnostic fit.

evidence.title: GitHub survey: AI wave across software teams
evidence.note: Organizations with neutral AI stances were more likely to be described as having complex toolchains; adoption support varies substantially.

evidence.title: Stack Overflow 2026 AI trust gap
evidence.note: Enterprise software buyers face rising AI adoption alongside falling trust, increasing governance and tool-selection complexity.
